name: Idiopathic Malabsorption Due to Bile Acid Synthesis Defects

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Bile Acid Synthesis Defects

criteria.description: Presence of chronic malabsorption symptoms including steatorrhea and failure to thrive
Detection of abnormal bile acid intermediates in plasma or urine by mass spectrometry
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in bile acid synthesis (e.g., HSD3B7, AKR1D1)
Exclusion of other causes of malabsorption such as celiac disease or pancreatic insufficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical malabsorption symptoms plus abnormal bile acid profile and genetic confirmation of bile acid synthesis defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent progressive liver disease and neurological complications.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of fat malabsorption due to bile acid deficiency
Manifested by elevated liver enzymes and jaundice
searchTerms: liver problems causing bile flow issues

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive or poor weight gain
common.notes: Due to chronic malabsorption and nutrient deficiency

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: Leading to secondary complications such as coagulopathy or bone disease
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.notes: Persistent loose stools due to malabsorption
Enlarged liver on physical exam or imaging

occasional.notes: Yellowing of skin and sclera due to cholestasis
Itching related to bile acid accumulation

rare.symptomName: Neurological abnormalities including hypotonia and developmental delay
rare.notes: Secondary to vitamin E deficiency or liver failure
searchTerms: brain problems including low muscle tone and delayed development
neurological symptoms with hypotonia and delay

rare.notes: Progressive liver scarring in untreated cases

laboratory: Elevated serum liver transaminases and bilirubin
Abnormal bile acid intermediates detected by mass spectrometry
Low serum fat-soluble vitamin levels (A, D, E, K)
Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Signs of cholestasis or cirrhosis on liver imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in bile acid synthesis genes such as HSD3B7, AKR1D1, CYP7A1
other: Liver biopsy may show cholestatic hepatitis and bile duct proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Villous atrophy on small bowel biopsy

differentialDiagnoses.diseaseId: bile acid malabsorption due to ileal disease
distinguishingFeatures: History of ileal resection or Crohn's disease
Increased bile acid loss in stool

redFlags: Severe fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies causing neurological or bleeding complications
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
references: Setchell KD, et al. Bile acid synthesis defects: diagnosis and treatment. J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr. 2013.
Miyake Y, et al. Genetic defects in bile acid synthesis and their clinical implications. Hepatology. 2017.
Orphanet: Idiopathic malabsorption due to bile acid synthesis defects. ORPHA:84065.
